name: TinaCMS
title: Mica vs. TinaCMS
summary: TinaCMS offers visual click-to-edit, a hosted service and an editorial workflow with pull requests. It keeps an index of your content in a database. Mica has none, but it is experimental.

chooseMica.text: You do not want a database or an index for your content.
You use Git LFS, or a Git host other than GitHub.
You want to run the editor yourself in one container, behind any OpenID Connect provider.
You want Astro to read the content through Content Collections, with types.

chooseOther.text: You need an editor that is ready for production. Mica is experimental, not ready for production.
Editors should click on the page and edit it there. TinaCMS does this, also in Astro.
You want a hosted service (TinaCloud) with plans and support.
You want search, MDX components, or an editorial workflow with draft pull requests.

facts.value: Yes. GitHub only, with TinaCloud and with the self-hosted provider. Custom providers are possible.
The local dev server works without the cloud. Editing in production needs TinaCloud, or a self-hosted backend: a backend function, a database adapter, a Git provider and an auth provider.
Yes. The Data Layer indexes your content. TinaCloud hosts it. Self-hosted needs MongoDB or Redis/Vercel KV.
Apache-2.0. The Data Layer packages have a separate licence. Free for 2 users. Team $24 a month for each project. Team Plus $41. Business $249. Enterprise on request.
Official @tinacms/astro. Astro is the default starter. Content comes through a generated GraphQL client, not Content Collections. It needs an SSR adapter.
TinaCloud: GitHub or email. SSO on Enterprise. Self-hosted: Auth.js, Clerk, TinaCloud or custom. OIDC is not documented.
Each save is a commit. The Editorial Workflow (Business and up) uses a branch and a draft pull request. No batch publish.
Yes. Visual click-to-edit, also in Astro.
Not supported. The documentation names limits of the GitHub API.
Not documented. localContentPath points local development to a separate content repository.
Not documented. The reference field links to collections. Large collections can time out.
Documented patterns, by directory or by field. No locale switcher.
TinaCloud has Admin and Editor. More roles on paid plans. Review is the Editorial Workflow with pull requests (Business).
An MCP server and AI features are listed as Coming Soon.
